title: Yoga's journey west
hook: retreat or show up? Arjuna asks which one is yoga
tomorrow: a book full of poses says they're only stairs. to where?

segments.voice: Yesterday, yoga's journey west started with one line: the posture is steady and easy, a seat. Today, a book that argues about what yoga is for.

Two kinds of advice turn up in a hard season. Log off, go quiet, retreat. Or: get to work, show up, keep going. Arjuna asks Krishna almost exactly this in the Bhagavad Gita. You praise giving up action, he says, and then you praise the yoga of action. Tell me plainly which one is better.
screen: `RETREAT, OR SHOW UP?` → `ARJUNA ASKS KRISHNA.` → `TELL ME PLAINLY WHICH.`

segments.voice: Both answers have a home in the Gita. First, the case for sitting apart. In chapter six, Krishna describes the yogi in a clean, quiet place, on a seat neither too high nor too low, body and head held steady, gaze resting toward the tip of the nose, the mind gathered in. And the tradition honors the sannyasin, who steps out of busy life altogether. Its best case: a scattered mind can't see clearly, so first you step out and get still. Now the case for acting. In chapter two Krishna says samatvam yoga uchyate: evenness is called yoga. Stay the same in success and failure, and act. Two verses later: yoga is skill in action. Its best case: life doesn't pause, duties don't wait, and a stillness that only works in a quiet room isn't finished yet. Krishna's own answer, in chapter five, is that both lead to the highest good, though of the two, he says, the yoga of action is better. Then he adds that only the unwise speak of the two as separate. So the Gita carries both: the quiet seat and the busy day.
screen: `THE CASE FOR THE QUIET SEAT.` · `THE CASE FOR EVENNESS IN ACTION.` · `BOTH LEAD TO THE HIGHEST GOOD.` · `ONLY THE UNWISE SPLIT THEM.`

segments.voice: Close your eyes and let the in-breath and the out-breath grow even, neither one winning. When a thought arrives labeled good or bad, let it land on that evenness without tipping you. Stay level, breath after breath.
Yoga's journey west: today through the Gita, where yoga is evenness, skill in action, and a quiet seat too.
Your line: yoga's journey west. Evenness is called yoga, on the mat and off it. Back tomorrow.

howItsDone: Hindu readers of the Gita find both paths in it: some take up sitting practice in a quiet place, as chapter six describes, and some treat their daily work as yoga, as chapters two and five teach.
